scope: CI3 credential boundary adjudication and media-stream error normalization. No claim of exhaustive penetration testing, actual personal credential exposure or new native/OS storage verification.

finding.location: src/main/media.ts registerMedia returned ReadableStream pull/cancel callbacks
finding.reproduction: A controlled upstream Error with a synthetic credential marker reaches the actual proxy Response body consumer through both reader.read rejection and reader.cancel rejection.
finding.boundary: Actual current media module and standard Response/ReadableStream with captured protocol registration and substituted upstream. It establishes forwarding at the protocol-response boundary, not that Chromium displays the upstream message.

fix: Normalize a read rejection to fixed retry guidance without an upstream cause. On cancellation, remove the active controller, abort upstream and contain reader.cancel rejection. Successful byte/range flow and existing status/redirect/revocation behavior remain unchanged.

conclusion: Eight credential obligations now have an explicit current review. A real unsanitized protocol error-forwarding path is fixed. CI3 is supported within controlled/current-source and retained native/OS scopes; Q13 still requires remaining invariants and full requirement adjudication.
limits: Synthetic marker, protocol capture and substituted upstream/preview/prepared adapters. No real provider/server request or personal token/key used.
Raw upstream exception forwarding at a Response body consumer is reproduced; actual Chromium error-display disclosure is not observed or asserted.
The proxy accepts valid media bytes as supplied; this is not proof against a malicious provider intentionally placing credentials in valid content.
No broad fuzzing, compromised-OS/renderer, arbitrary corruption, forced power loss or full codec validation claim.
Historical OS/native records retain their exact process/source/substitution scopes. Current source composition is not a fresh native replay of every older test.
No observed listener, audible-quality, VoiceOver, hardware, deferred smaller-window or enlarged-zoom result.
